From: Priya Desai <priya@orwellhealth.com>

Subject: SIG: Clarify GPU tenant isolation for Dedicated

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the quick SIG intake last week. As part of our procurement review we need a few follow-ups specifically around Dedicated GPU tenancy and noisy-neighbor risk. A few concrete questions from our security team: 

- Do you co-locate multiple customers on the same physical GPU (or MIG partition) in Dedicated? If so, under what policy?
- What technical controls guard against noisy-neighbor impact (CPU/GPU scheduling, memory/PCIe isolation, QoS)?
- Do you have tenant-level tagging in process metadata and in the kernel/audit logs we can sample?
- Can you provide a short diagram or artifact that shows how a customer workload is isolated from others (network, storage, process namespaces)?

We are working to close the SIG v1.7 items and ideally would like artifacts by EOD Thursday (Mar 26). If any of this requires an NDA or redacted outputs that’s fine — let us know.

Best,
Priya
Priya Desai
Head of Security — Orwell Health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya@orwellhealth.com>
Cc: Carl Thomson <carl.thomson@orwellhealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: Clarify GPU tenant isolation for Dedicated

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by the artifacts I’ve attached (redwood_SIG_gpu_addendum.pdf) with config snippets and screenshots: 

- Co-location policy: Redwood Dedicated allocates GPU capacity at the allocation unit level. Where hardware supports MIG (NVIDIA A100/A30 families) we may provision multiple isolated MIG instances on a single GPU only when customers explicitly purchase MIG-shared SKUs; for standard Dedicated pools we prefer exclusive GPU assignment per allocation (exclusive mode) to minimize cross-tenant contention.

- Noisy-neighbor mitigations: we use a combination of (1) exclusive GPU assignment or MIG partitions with strict resource quotas, (2) runtime cgroups and CPU pinning to constrain host CPU usage, (3) PCIe bandwidth shaping and NVLink isolation where available, and (4) priority-aware scheduler with preemption windows for short-lived jobs. We also apply auto-throttling on per-queue token rates to limit burst effects.

- Tenant tagging & audit evidence: all inference jobs are tagged at submission with tenant_id and route_id. Tags propagate into the orchestration metadata, container labels, and are present in our audit-event stream (process start / container create events). I’ve included a redacted audit sample and a screenshot of the tenant tag shown in the orchestration UI (kv-tagging-snapshot.png).

- Network/storage/process separation: Dedicated runs customer workloads in isolated network namespaces inside VPC-to-VPC peering (private ENI or SR-IOV where configured). Storage volumes are tenant-scoped with ACLs; local ephemeral GPU-backed storage is isolated by container namespaces and unique tmpfs mounts. The attached addendum contains a compact diagram and the snippet showing namespace and iptable rules.

I attached: redwood_SIG_gpu_addendum.pdf (diagram + config excerpts), kv-tagging-snapshot.png (orchestration UI tag), sched-config-snippet.txt (scheduler QoS snippet). If you prefer, we can also provide a short recorded walkthrough or host a 30-min technical call with our infra/security leads.

Requested delivery timeline: we can provide the redacted artifacts now and a one-hour sample of audit events within 48 hours. Let me know what level of redaction you need.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Kimberly — this is helpful, thank you. A few follow-ups from our security reviewers: 

1) Can you attach a short network diagram (redacted is fine) showing VPC boundaries and where Dedicated nodes sit relative to our private peering?
2) For the audit sample: we need a 30–60 minute window showing process/container create events with tenant tags; the tenant_id can be redacted but timestamps and event types must be real.
3) For the scheduler QoS snippet: can you include the EXACT config lines you run in production (you can strip comments/keys) or provide a redacted example with the same fields?

Also, we need to confirm whether any Dedicated SKU uses MIG-shared partitions by default (we need an explicit list of SKUs that do). Our procurement will likely insist on exclusive-mode by default.

If you can deliver artifacts by Thu EOD that would be great — otherwise let us know the earliest slot. If it helps we can sign an NDA for more detailed logs.

Thanks,
Priya
